title: The First Week I Endured
description:
During the first week on the job, {name} held on — 'this is the best option right now.'

That first week feels distant.

At the end of a similarly hard day today, that earlier self came to mind.

choices.text: Enduring then became the foundation now
choices.result_text:
'Best option' can sound shabby. But those shabby best-options stacked into a path.

Because the first week was endured, there was a second week, and so on to here.
{name} acknowledged that persistence anew.

choices.text: Now I do more than just endure
choices.result_text:
The enduring phase is past.

{name} no longer merely holds on — they design what's next.
The first-week self would have been amazed at how far the view had widened.

title: The Work Itself Was Fine
description:
During the first week, {name} unexpectedly felt 'the work itself was fine.'

That feeling resurfaces sometimes.

A moment of unexpected satisfaction in work they'd seen only as a means to money.

choices.text: Finding meaning in work isn't bad either
choices.result_text:
See every hour only as a means to Gangnam and five years is too long.

If you can find small reward in the work itself, the road hurts less.
{name} was finding a balance between means and process.

choices.text: Still, the goal is elsewhere — don't forget
choices.result_text:
Even if the work is good, this isn't the destination.

{name} decided not to settle into satisfaction.
What you enjoy and where you must go can differ — they remembered that coldly.

title: The First Week I Doubted
description:
During the first week, {name} was plagued by doubt — 'is this right?'

Has the doubt vanished, or just grown familiar?

Today the question surfaced again.

choices.text: Doubting yet continuing was the answer
choices.result_text:
Doubt wasn't something to erase but to carry.

Had they quit then, there'd be no foundation now.
{name} acknowledged the self who stepped forward even within doubt.

choices.text: Re-examine whether that doubt was right
choices.result_text:
Neither ignoring doubt nor being swept by it is the answer.

{name} turned the doubt into data and checked it.
Finding answers by numbers, not emotion — that first week taught it.

title: First Paycheck, Opening the App
description:
The day of the first paycheck, instead of celebrating, {name} immediately opened the investing app. 'This money can't just sit in the account.'

That instinct built the current momentum.

Money came in again today.

choices.text: That mindset — make money work
choices.result_text:
Knew from the first payday that salary alone can't reach Gangnam.

Money making money. {name} grasped it early, started early.
That one month's head start becomes a large gap five years out.

choices.text: Now I watch risk over speed
choices.result_text:
At first, believed rolling it all was the answer.

Now knows not losing matters as much as gaining.
{name}'s investing had matured from offense to balance.

title: When the Overtime Piled Up
description:
As overtime accumulated, {name} thought, 'this job isn't my answer — find another direction.'

The result of that thought is the present.

That judgment came to mind today.

choices.text: Doubting the direction was right — I've changed paths
choices.result_text:
A career filled by overtime has a ceiling.

Seeing that limit early, {name} prepared another path.
Changing direction wasn't giving up — it was strategy.

choices.text: The job's still a safety net — watch the balance
choices.result_text:
Sought another direction, but didn't carelessly toss the net underfoot.

{name} planned what's next from atop the foundation of a job.
Taking risk and being reckless are different.

title: The First Stop-Loss
description:
Facing the first investment loss, {name} cut it — 'better to get out before losing more.'

The sting of that first stop-loss.

Today they stood at a similar fork.

choices.text: A stop-loss isn't defeat — it's discipline
choices.result_text:
Most people hold on trying not to lose, and lose more.

The discipline learned at the first stop-loss saved {name} several times.
Knowing when to cut was a surviving investor's first condition.

choices.text: This time, set the stop-loss line in advance
choices.result_text:
Cut by emotion and you're always late.

{name} drew the exit line before entering.
The first stop-loss's pain was tuition that built a principle.

title: The First Loss I Held Through
description:
Facing the first investment loss, {name} held on — 'like Sang-chul said, the market always comes back.'

How did holding turn out?

Today paper losses glow red again.

choices.text: Holding on principle was right — don't waver
choices.result_text:
Not selling in fear.

That simple principle was learned in the body at the first loss.
{name} watched the red numbers, and this time the hands didn't shake.

choices.text: Holding and stubbornness differ — recheck the basis
choices.result_text:
Holding blindly is gambling.

{name} first re-examined whether the original reason for buying still held.
If the basis lives, hold; if it's broken, cut. That was the difference.

title: The First Loss I Averaged Down
description:
Facing the first investment loss, {name} averaged down — 'buy more to lower the cost basis.'

Was that choice medicine or poison?

Today the same temptation rises before a losing position.

choices.text: Averaging down needs conviction — be careful
choices.result_text:
Only with conviction it'll rise does averaging down become medicine.

{name} learned then that averaging down without basis only grows the loss.
This time, they re-examined the fundamentals first.

choices.text: This time, choose the stop-loss over averaging down
choices.result_text:
Catch a falling knife and you only cut your hand.

{name} knows the sweet temptation of averaging down. So they guarded against it more.
That earlier lesson made a different choice today.

title: The Night I Studied Till 2 a.m.
description:
In the goshiwon days, even after Hyun-su went to sleep, {name} studied until 2 a.m.

Those dawns stacked into the present.

Tonight too, sitting at the desk late.

choices.text: Those dawns weren't wasted
choices.result_text:
A light left on while others slept.

Those hours built an invisible gap.
{name} knows they owe a lot to the dawn self.

choices.text: Cut the reckless all-nighters now — watch efficiency
choices.result_text:
All-nighters powered by desperation were needed, but can't last forever.

{name} began to value quality of time over quantity.
To go long, you learn to warm rather than burn.

title: The Day I Organized a Year's Records
description:
In the first year in Seoul, {name} organized a year of records to 'confirm in numbers how far I'd come.'

That habit continued.

Today they opened those records again.

choices.text: Records steady me when I waver
choices.result_text:
Emotion lies that 'nothing has changed,' but records don't lie.

The numbers compared to a year ago gave {name} objective comfort.
Seeing how far you've come shows how much farther to go.

choices.text: Beyond records — design the next year
choices.result_text:
Didn't stop at writing down the road traveled.

{name} used that data to plan the next year's strategy.
Records were both a summary of the past and a map of the future.

title: Year One Was the Warm-up
description:
In the first year in Seoul, {name} vowed, 'year one was the warm-up — push harder.'

That ferocity carried all the way here.

That vow came to mind today.

choices.text: That ferocity dragged me this far
choices.result_text:
Even the year called a warm-up was a full sprint to someone.

Pushing that hard produced a speed unlike others'.
{name} didn't regret the ferocity.

choices.text: Ferocity alone won't last — pace it sustainably
choices.result_text:
Early explosive drive was needed. But five years isn't a sprint.

{name} converted ferocity into a sustainable pace.
Going all the way belongs not to the fastest but to those who don't stop.

title: Using the Job as a Base
description:
Feeling the career ceiling, {name} decided 'I'll keep the job' and use it as a base of stability.

The result of that choice is the present.

Today they look back on that judgment.

choices.text: Stable cash flow made the risk-taking possible
choices.result_text:
With a salary coming in monthly, they could avoid overreaching in investing.

A challenge with a safety net differs from one without.
{name} jumped farther using the job as a springboard.

choices.text: Now I look past the job — to the next stage
choices.result_text:
Even a job used as a base must one day be graduated from.

{name} didn't forget the job was a tool, not a purpose.
Once sturdy enough, the time comes to move to the next stage.

title: Wanting to Move Bigger
description:
Feeling the career ceiling, {name} thought 'I have to move bigger' and considered switching jobs or another path.

Did that resolve become action?

That ambition came to mind today.

choices.text: That resolve set me in motion
choices.result_text:
Didn't stop at admitting the limit — aimed past it.

Had they settled into the present, they'd have stayed at the ceiling.
{name} felt the resolve to draw a bigger picture had been right.

choices.text: Move big but not recklessly — calculate
choices.result_text:
Ambition is good, but ambition without calculation is gambling.

{name} balanced 'bigger' against 'smarter.'
The bigger the move, the more firmly you must watch your footing.

title: Promising to Get It Together
description:
When job and investing clashed, {name} held the job for now, telling the boss 'I'm sorry, I'll get it together.'

They think of that choice sometimes.

Today the boss said in passing, 'Doing good work lately.'

choices.text: "Glad I steadied myself back then."
choices.result_text:
Had they lost the job to investing distraction, even the safety net would have collapsed.

Holding the job then was the choice that kept the balance.
{name} learned to catch both rabbits that day.

choices.text: Inwardly — no longer bound to the job alone
choices.result_text:
A loyal employee on the surface, a person heading toward their own goal underneath.

{name} ran that dual track more skillfully now.
Keep the job — but don't mortgage your life to it.
